artworks.title: The Prophecy of Calchas (from The Story of Troy)
artworks.description: A silk-and-gilt tapestry from a Macao-woven Troy cycle (Metropolitan Museum of Art, 50.97.2): Calchas reads the omens that bind the Achaean war — the seer of Aulis and the Iliad rendered for a Renaissance collector's wall.

artworks.title: Calchas as Haruspex (Etruscan bronze mirror)
artworks.description: An Etruscan engraved mirror names Calchas (Chalchas) as a winged haruspex reading a liver — the Greek mantis recast in Italian ritual guise, proof of how early the Trojan seer travelled west of the Adriatic.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Bourdon's Aulis canvas gathers the priestly circle around the altar where Calchas names Artemis' price — the seer whose reading turns Agamemnon's fleet into a daughter's death.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia (Pompeii fresco)
artworks.description: A peristyle fresco from Pompeii (Naples, MAN 9112) shows Calchas at the sacrifice of Iphigenia — the Homeric prophet as the ritual hinge that buys the winds for Troy.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Petersen's war council keeps a Homeric prophet at Agamemnon's ear — Calchas as the voice that reads gods into strategy.

films.title: Iphigenia
films.description: At Aulis, Calchas names the goddess's price — Cacoyannis makes the seer's reading the hinge of the sacrifice.

popCulture.title: Calchas
popCulture.description: Thestor's son who foresaw Troy's fall and his own death at a wiser seer's hands — Homer's chief Achaean prophet.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Calchas names Chryses' insult and Apollo's plague — the seer whose omens open the wrath and whose Colophon contest closes the cycle.
